hydration.name: Hydration
hydration.blurb: Water, and a reason to stand up.

breaks.name: Look far away
breaks.instruction: Find the farthest thing you can see. Let your eyes soften.
steps: Look away from your screen at something at least 20 feet away. Out a window is ideal.
Focus on it for 20 seconds. Let the detail go and just hold the distance.
Blink a few times before you come back to the screen.
breaks.tip: Distance is what relaxes the focusing muscle. Scrolling on your phone keeps it clenched.

breaks.name: Blink reset
breaks.instruction: Blink slowly ten times, then squeeze your eyes shut for two seconds.
steps: Keep looking at the screen, or close your eyes, it doesn't matter.
Blink slowly and completely ten times. Feel the eyelid meet the lower lid each time.
Finish with your eyes squeezed gently shut for two seconds, then open.
breaks.tip: People blink about a third as often at a screen. Dry, gritty eyes are usually just missed blinks.

breaks.name: Palming
breaks.instruction: Cup your palms over closed eyes and breathe in the dark.
steps: Rub your palms together until they feel warm.
Close your eyes and cup your palms over them without pressing on the eyeballs.
Let your fingers rest on your forehead and the heels of your hands on your cheekbones.
Breathe slowly in the dark for 45 seconds.
breaks.tip: The point is darkness and rest, not pressure. If you see light through your fingers, your hands aren't cupped enough.

breaks.name: Eye circles
breaks.instruction: Roll your eyes in slow, easy circles. Reverse halfway.
steps: Look up, then slowly trace a big circle with your eyes: up, right, down, left.
Make four slow circles clockwise, blinking whenever you need to.
Switch direction and make four circles the other way.
breaks.tip: Keep it slow and stop if you feel a headache coming on. Fast eye movements are not the goal.

breaks.name: Sip of water
breaks.instruction: Drink a full glass of water. Slowly, away from your screen.
steps: Pick up your glass or bottle and take a few slow sips.
Keep your eyes off the screen while you drink.
Finish the glass if you can. If it's empty, that's your refill cue.
breaks.tip: Mild dehydration feels a lot like afternoon brain fog. Water first, coffee second.

breaks.name: Refill your bottle
breaks.instruction: Get up, walk to the water, and refill. Leave your phone.
steps: Stand up and take your bottle or glass to the nearest water source.
Refill it. Take the long way back if you can.
Set it down where you'll see it, then sit back down.
breaks.tip: This is a two-for-one: hydration plus a short walk plus a break from the screen.

breaks.name: Water by the window
breaks.instruction: Sip water while you look out a window for a minute.
steps: Take a glass of water to the nearest window or the furthest view in the room.
Drink slowly while you look at something distant.
Try to notice three things outside or across the room before you return.
breaks.tip: Combines hydration with the 20-20-20 eye reset. Good one when you're too busy for a walk.

breaks.name: Box breathing
breaks.instruction: In for 4, hold 4, out for 4, hold 4. Five rounds.
steps: Sit tall and let your shoulders drop.
Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.
Hold for 4. Breathe out slowly for 4. Hold empty for 4.
Repeat for five rounds, or until the timer ends.
breaks.tip: If 4 seconds feels long, use 3. The even rhythm matters more than the number.

breaks.name: Physiological sigh
breaks.instruction: Two inhales through the nose, then one long sigh out. Three times.
steps: Breathe in through your nose until your lungs feel about 80% full.
Add a second short sniff of air on top, without exhaling first.
Let it all out through your mouth in a long, slow sigh.
Do three of these.
breaks.tip: The double inhale reinflates tiny air sacs and the long exhale slows your heart. Fastest reset there is.

breaks.name: 4-7-8 breathing
breaks.instruction: In for 4, hold for 7, out for 8. Four rounds.
steps: Sit back and rest your tongue behind your top front teeth.
Breathe in through your nose for 4.
Hold for 7. Then breathe out through your mouth for 8.
Repeat four times.
breaks.tip: If you get lightheaded, shorten the counts. Don't force a bigger breath than is comfortable.

breaks.name: Five-senses reset
breaks.instruction: Name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste.
steps: Look around and silently name five things you can see.
Notice four things you can feel: your feet, the chair, your sleeves, the air.
Listen for three sounds. Then two smells, then one taste.
Take one slow breath before you go back.
breaks.tip: This pulls attention out of the task loop and into your body. Useful when you're stuck or frazzled.

breaks.name: Chin tucks
breaks.instruction: Slide your head straight back, like a double chin.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and your eyes looking straight ahead.
Without tipping your head up or down, glide your chin straight back. Yes, it gives you a double chin.
Hold for 2 or 3 seconds. You should feel a gentle stretch where your skull meets your neck.
Let your head glide forward to neutral. That's one rep.
breaks.tip: Keep your eyes level the whole time. If you're nodding down, you're doing a different move.

breaks.name: Doorway stretch
breaks.instruction: Forearms on a door frame, lean through gently.
steps: Stand in an open doorway. Raise your arms so your elbows are at shoulder height and bent to about 90 degrees.
Rest your forearms flat on each side of the frame, palms facing forward.
Step one foot through and slowly lean forward until you feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Hold for 30 seconds and breathe normally. Step back to release.
breaks.tip: Aim for a gentle stretch, not a strain, and don't let your lower back arch. No doorway nearby? Do one arm at a time against a wall corner.

breaks.name: Scap squeezes
breaks.instruction: Pinch your shoulder blades back and down, then let go.
steps: Sit or stand tall. Let your arms hang, or bend your elbows to about 90 degrees if that's easier.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and slightly down, like you're pinching a pencil between them.
Hold for 2 seconds.
Relax completely, then repeat. Do 15.
breaks.tip: Don't shrug your shoulders up toward your ears or push your ribs forward. The move is small and happens in your upper back.

breaks.name: Walkaround
breaks.instruction: Get up and walk. Refill your water, rest your eyes.
steps: Stand up and walk anywhere for 2 minutes. A lap around the room or a water refill both count.
Let your arms swing and your shoulders drop.
On the way, look at something at least 20 feet away for about 20 seconds to give your eyes a break.
breaks.tip: Leave your phone at the desk. This one only works if your eyes get a break too.

breaks.name: Thoracic extension
breaks.instruction: Hands behind your head, arch back over your chair.
steps: Sit all the way back so the top of your chair's backrest touches your mid back, just below your shoulder blades.
Lace your fingers behind your head with your elbows pointing forward. Your hands support your neck, they don't pull it.
Gently lean back over the backrest, lifting your chest toward the ceiling.
Pause for a breath, then sit back up. Do 10.
breaks.tip: Bend from your upper back, not your lower back or neck. If your chair reclines or rolls, brace it against something first or skip this one.

breaks.name: Hip flexor stretch
breaks.instruction: Split stance, tuck your hips and push them forward.
steps: Stand with one foot a big step in front of the other, both feet pointing forward. Hold your desk if you want.
Bend your front knee a little and keep your back leg long.
Tuck your tailbone under by squeezing the glute on your back leg, then gently shift your hips forward.
You should feel it at the front of your back hip. Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.
breaks.tip: Keep your chest tall. Arching your lower back to go deeper just moves the stretch somewhere it doesn't help.

breaks.name: Neck side stretch
breaks.instruction: Ear toward shoulder, other shoulder stays down.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your head to bring your right ear toward your right shoulder. Keep looking forward.
Keep your left shoulder down. For a little more, reach your left hand toward the floor.
Hold for 20 seconds, come back to center slowly, then do the other side.
breaks.tip: Don't lift your shoulder up to meet your ear, and don't pull on your head with your hand.

breaks.name: Calf raises
breaks.instruction: Rise up onto your toes, lower slowly.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Rest a hand on your desk or a wall for balance.
Press through the balls of your feet and rise up as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly, taking about 2 seconds, until your heels touch down. Do 20.
breaks.tip: Keep your weight over your big toes so your ankles don't roll outward.

breaks.name: Shoulder rolls
breaks.instruction: Roll your shoulders back in big, slow circles.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed.
Lift your shoulders toward your ears, roll them back, then let them drop.
Make ten slow circles backward.
Reverse and make ten forward.
breaks.tip: Big and slow beats fast and small. Let your shoulder blades actually move.

breaks.name: Wrist release
breaks.instruction: Stretch your fingers, then flex each wrist gently.
steps: Spread your fingers wide and hold for three seconds. Make a loose fist, then spread again.
Turn your right palm up and use your left hand to gently draw the fingers down.
Switch hands. Then shake both hands out for a few seconds.
breaks.tip: Keep the stretch gentle. If you feel tingling or numbness, stop and mention it to a doctor.

breaks.name: Desk push-ups
breaks.instruction: Hands on the desk, lower your chest, press back.
steps: Stand an arm's length from your desk and put both palms on the edge, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the desk.
Press back up. Do 10, keeping your core braced and your neck long.
breaks.tip: Make sure the desk can't slide. If it has wheels, brace it against a wall first.

breaks.name: Stand and reach
breaks.instruction: Stand tall, reach overhead, then lean gently side to side.
steps: Stand up and reach both arms toward the ceiling.
Take a breath in and lengthen through your ribs.
Lean a few inches to the left, then to the right, like a slow pendulum.
Let your arms come down and shake them out.
breaks.tip: Keep your ribs stacked over your hips instead of arching your lower back.
